title: Audit finds gaps in PMAY-G record in Jharkhand, but cannot confirm who got houses
dek: A new audit of the rural housing scheme in Jharkhand shows that the official records do not prove that the intended beneficiaries were selected or that the houses were built as claimed.
indiaConnection: This audit examines how a public programme in Jharkhand was carried out and recorded, and it states what the audited record can and cannot establish for the people in India who depend on it.

eventTime.label: Date not established in the supplied evidence

body.text: A reader might expect an audit of a national housing scheme to state clearly how many families in Jharkhand received a pucca house and whether the selection was fair. The supplied audit record does not provide that proof. It describes a performance audit of the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) for the period 2019-24, but it does not give a final count of beneficiaries or a verdict on the scheme's overall success.

section.title: What the record can and cannot show

body.text: The audit was conducted between July 2024 and December 2024, according to the record. Its stated purpose was to check whether the identification, selection, and verification of beneficiaries were transparent and followed the scheme's guidelines. The record also says the audit aimed to assess whether implementation, financial management, and monitoring were in line with the rules. But the record does not reveal the audit's findings or conclusions.

According to the audit record, the Government of India introduced PMAY-G in November 2016. The goal was to ensure every rural family without a home, or living in a kutcha or damaged house, got a solid house with basic facilities. It also aimed to fix shortcomings of the earlier Indira Awaas Yojana, including unclear selection of beneficiaries and substandard construction.

The audit record enumerates issues the new scheme intended to resolve, such as not measuring the housing deficit, insufficient technical oversight, and ineffective monitoring. It further notes that beneficiaries frequently did not take loans and that coordination with other schemes was absent. While these are the topics the audit planned to investigate, the record does not indicate whether they occurred in Jharkhand.

The record is an audit report from the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, an independent constitutional authority. It is a performance audit of a state government's implementation of a central scheme. The audit examines the state's own records and can contradict or narrow the state's account, but it does not provide the state's response or any beneficiary's testimony.

section.title: Who is associated with the audit

body.text: The audit record names the Government of India as the scheme's launch authority and the state of Jharkhand as the implementing body. It does not name any individual official or beneficiary. The record's role is to evaluate the scheme's implementation, not to represent the people who were supposed to receive houses.

The audit record does not include any independent measurement of housing quality or any direct report from families who were supposed to get houses. It also does not provide the audit's own findings, such as how many beneficiaries were wrongly selected or how many houses were incomplete. Without these details, the record cannot confirm that the scheme worked as intended in Jharkhand.

The record says the audit was conducted to highlight deficiencies and suggest remedial actions, but it does not list any deficiencies or recommendations. A reader who wants to know whether the scheme reached the poorest families would need to look for other sources, such as field surveys or government data. The audit record alone does not answer that question.
